title: Extension of scalars is left adjoint to restriction
statement:
In the situation of [def-sfb-modobj-extension], let
$u_M\colon M\to\mathcal S\otimes_{\mathcal R}M$ be the composite
$M\cong\mathbf 1\otimes M\xrightarrow{\eta_{\mathcal S}\otimes M}\mathcal S\otimes M
\to\mathcal S\otimes_{\mathcal R}M$. Then $u_M$ is $\mathcal R$-linear into
$\operatorname{Res}_\varphi(\mathcal S\otimes_{\mathcal R}M)$
([def-sfb-modobj-restriction]). Moreover, $g\mapsto\operatorname{Res}_\varphi(g)\circ u_M$
is a bijection, natural in $M$ and $N$, from $\mathcal S$-linear maps
$\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi M\to N$ to $\mathcal R$-linear maps
$M\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi N$. This is an adjunction
$$
\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi\dashv\operatorname{Res}_\varphi .
$$

proof.text: Use the hypotheses and construction of [def-sfb-modobj-extension]. Put $Q_M=\mathcal S\otimes_{\mathcal R}M$, and write $p_M:\mathcal S\otimes M\to Q_M$ for the coequalizer of $a_M=(\mu_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal S\otimes\varphi))\otimes M$ and $b_M=(\mathcal S\otimes\gamma_M)\alpha_{\mathcal S,\mathcal R,M}$. Write $\delta_M:\mathcal S\otimes Q_M\to Q_M$ for its action. Unpacking "acting on the first factor" in that node gives $\delta_M(\mathcal S\otimes p_M)=p_M m_M$, where $m_M=(\mu_{\mathcal S}\otimes M)\alpha^{-1}_{\mathcal S,\mathcal S,M}$. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], applied to the finite parallel-pair diagram (Stacks Tags 002A, 002F), gives both descent and cancellation: if $vp_M=wp_M$, both $v,w$ factor the same cocone and uniqueness gives $v=w$. Since $\mathcal S\otimes-$ preserves colimits by hypothesis, $\mathcal S\otimes p_M$ is a coequalizer of the image parallel pair and has the same cancellation property. In subsequent displayed composites, the canonical associators and unitors are suppressed; inserting them uses their naturality and the tensor interchange law.

source.place: Paragraphs 1–2: the projection and its coequalizer universal property; Stacks Categories, definition-coequalizers (002A), definition-colimit (002F)

proof.text:
The module laws and the meaning of a linear map are those of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Let $i_M=(\eta_{\mathcal S}\otimes M)\lambda_M^{-1}$, so $u_M=p_M i_M$. Precompose $p_Mb_M=p_Ma_M$ with insertion of $\eta_{\mathcal S}$ before $\mathcal R\otimes M$. The left unit law of $\mathcal S$ gives
$$u_M\gamma_M=p_M(\mathcal S\otimes\gamma_M)(\eta_{\mathcal S}\otimes\mathcal R\otimes M)=p_M(\mu_{\mathcal S}(\eta_{\mathcal S}\otimes\varphi)\otimes M)=p_M(\varphi\otimes M).$$
On the other hand the action identity of step 1 and the right unit law give
$$\delta_M(\varphi\otimes Q_M)(\mathcal R\otimes u_M)=p_M(\mu_{\mathcal S}\otimes M)(\varphi\otimes\eta_{\mathcal S}\otimes M)=p_M(\varphi\otimes M).$$
The restricted action is $\delta_M(\varphi\otimes Q_M)$ by [def-sfb-modobj-restriction]. These two equations are precisely its required $\mathcal R$-linearity equation for $u_M$.

source.place: Paragraph 1: the two computations proving linearity of the unit

proof.text:
Fix an $\mathcal S$-module $N$ and an $\mathcal R$-linear $f:M\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi N$. By [def-sfb-modobj-restriction] and [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], $f\gamma_M=\gamma_N(\varphi\otimes N)(\mathcal R\otimes f)$. Define $h_f=\gamma_N(\mathcal S\otimes f):\mathcal S\otimes M\to N$. Substituting this equation and then the associativity law for the action on $N$ gives
$$h_f b_M=\gamma_N(\mathcal S\otimes(f\gamma_M))\alpha=\gamma_N(\mu_{\mathcal S}\otimes N)(\mathcal S\otimes\varphi\otimes f)=h_f a_M.$$
Thus $h_f$ coequalizes exactly the pair defining $Q_M$ in [def-sfb-modobj-extension]; this is a calculation of morphisms in $\mathcal C$, requiring no elementwise description of $M$ or $N$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, first two sentences: the balancing calculation

proof.text:
By the coequalizer universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] (Stacks Tags 002A, 002F), step 3 gives a unique underlying morphism $\bar f:Q_M\to N$ with $\bar f p_M=h_f$. It is $\mathcal S$-linear: using the action of [def-sfb-modobj-extension] and the associativity law of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects],
$$\bar f\delta_M(\mathcal S\otimes p_M)=h_f m_M=\gamma_N(\mathcal S\otimes h_f)=\gamma_N(\mathcal S\otimes\bar f)(\mathcal S\otimes p_M).$$
For the middle equality, both sides are $\gamma_N(\mu_{\mathcal S}\otimes N)(\mathcal S\otimes\mathcal S\otimes f)$ after reassociation. Cancel $\mathcal S\otimes p_M$ using the uniqueness argument of step 1. The resulting equation $\bar f\delta_M=\gamma_N(\mathcal S\otimes\bar f)$ is exactly linearity.

source.place: Paragraph 2: descent and the asserted S-linearity, expanded

proof.text:
For an $\mathcal S$-linear $g:Q_M\to N$, define $\Phi_{M,N}(g)=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi(g)u_M$; restriction preserves linearity by [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], and the composite is linear by the morphism definition [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and step 2. Define $\Psi_{M,N}(f)=\bar f$ by step 4. Then
$$\Phi_{M,N}(\Psi_{M,N}(f))=\bar f u_M=h_f i_M=\gamma_N(\eta_{\mathcal S}\otimes N)\lambda_N^{-1} f=f,$$
where tensor interchange and naturality of $\lambda$ give the penultimate expression and the unit law on $N$ gives the last equality.

source.place: Paragraph 2, first inverse identity (the unit law)

proof.text:
The first-factor action of [def-sfb-modobj-extension] satisfies
$$\delta_M(\mathcal S\otimes u_M)=p_M(\mu_{\mathcal S}\otimes M)(\mathcal S\otimes\eta_{\mathcal S}\otimes M)=p_M$$
by the right unit law. Hence for an $\mathcal S$-linear $g$, using its linearity equation from [sk-def-sfb-module-objects],
$$h_{\Phi(g)}=\gamma_N(\mathcal S\otimes(g u_M))=g\delta_M(\mathcal S\otimes u_M)=g p_M.$$
Both $\Psi(\Phi(g))$ and $g$ therefore descend the same map $h_{\Phi(g)}$. Uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives $\Psi(\Phi(g))=g$. Together with step 5 this proves that the stated $\Phi$ is a bijection.

source.place: Paragraph 2, second inverse identity and uniqueness from the projection

proof.text:
For an $\mathcal R$-linear $a:M'\to M$, the map construction in [def-sfb-modobj-extension] gives $(\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi a)p_{M'}=p_M(\mathcal S\otimes a)$. Composing with $i_{M'}$ and using tensor interchange and naturality of $\lambda$ gives $(\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi a)u_{M'}=u_M a$. Consequently
$$\Phi_{M',N}(g\circ\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi a)=\Phi_{M,N}(g)\circ a.$$
For an $\mathcal S$-linear $b:N\to N'$, restriction is the identity on underlying morphisms and is a functor by [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], so associativity of composition gives
$$\Phi_{M,N'}(b\circ g)=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi(b)\circ\Phi_{M,N}(g).$$
These are the two naturality equations, with all source and target module structures fixed.

source.place: Paragraph 3: naturality in M and N, expanded into its two equations

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] with $F=\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi$, $G=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$, and hom-set bijections $\Phi_{M,N}$ from steps 5–6. Step 7 verifies both of its naturality hypotheses. This constructs $\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi\dashv\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ with exactly the hom bijection in the statement. Its unit is $\Phi_{M,Q_M}(\mathrm{id}_{Q_M})=u_M$, so it is the adjunction with the specified unit, rather than merely an unspecified adjunction between the same functors.

source.place: Paragraph 3 and the adjunction conclusion; Stacks Categories, definition-adjoint (0037) and following paragraph

lean.statement: noncomputable def extendRestrictAdjunction : extendScalars φ ⊣ comap φ
lean.note: Exact existing upstream construction, read locally and confirmed with scompile.py --source in the live repository. Uses precisely Mod.extendScalars from def-sfb-modobj-extension and Mathlib Mod.comap from def-sfb-modobj-restriction. Mod.extendUnitHom is the specified inverse left unitor, tensor of the S-unit with M, and coequalizer projection; Mod.extendUnit bundles its R-linearity. Mod.extendHomEquiv has forward map g ↦ extendUnit φ M ≫ (comap φ).map g, inverse extendHom φ, and both inverse laws. extendRestrictAdjunction is Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv of those very equivalences with both naturality laws. It therefore provides the specified unit and natural bijection, not merely an unspecified adjunction. The arbitrary object and morphism universes remain independent, only R is commutative, and no closedness or additivity hypothesis is imposed. The small-colimit preservation hypotheses are identical to those of the recorded extension functor; the node inherits those interfaces.
